front.title: Acts-For: Signing In to a Website with a ~handle, for a Person or an Agent Acting for One

abstract.t: Acts-For lets a person sign in to any website with the ~handle they already hold, and lets an AI agent sign in or register at that website on the person's behalf. Neither needs a username, a password or an account per site. A website joins by publishing one DNS record. A person signs in through a standard OpenID Connect authorization code flow and the site receives a short-lived token naming the person by a number unique to that site. An agent obtains a short-lived pass from the issuer over the Model Context Protocol and presents it to the site. The pass names the same per-site number, the agent's own key and ~handle, and the limits the person set. The site checks it against a published key and calls nobody.
